plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding exactly my true value ($30) is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, there's no benefit to shading my bid. I'll bid my true value of $30.

This is a second-price auction, so the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay (the second-highest bid), and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no benefit to bidding higher or lower than my true valuation of $7, as this could either cause me to overpay or miss profitable wins.

This is a second-price auction, so bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly $36 ensures I win whenever the second-highest bid is below my value (guaranteeing positive profit) and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding higher than 36 risks paying more than my value if I "win" against someone bidding between 36 and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, $36 is optimal.
